&nbsp;

**Subgraph:**

[$G'=(V',E')$ is a subgraph of $G=(V,E)$ iff $V'\subseteq V$ and $E'\subseteq E$ and $(u,v)\in E'\to u\in V'$ and $v\in V'$.]{style="color:#3c78d8; font-style:italic; font-size:0.82em"}

&nbsp;

**Degree(v):** [*number of edges that touch vertex v.*]{style="color:#3c78d8; font-style:italic"}

## Check Divisibility by 7 {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
1. Start at the circle node at the top.
2. For each digit $d$, follow $d$ blue (solid) edges, followed by 1 red (dashed) edge.
3. If you end up at the circle node, your number is divisible by 7.

> Example: **3703**

**Walk:** [*Sequence of vertices between which there are edges*]{style="color:#3c78d8; font-style:italic"}

**Trail:** [*Walk with no repeated edges*]{style="color:#3c78d8; font-style:italic"}

**Path(alt):** [*Walk with no repeated vertices*]{style="color:#3c78d8; font-style:italic"}

**Circuit:** [*Trail that begins and ends in same place*]{style="color:#3c78d8; font-style:italic"}

**Cycle:** [*Path that begins and ends in same place*]{style="color:#3c78d8; font-style:italic"}
:::
::: {.column width="30%"}
![](/images/gr6.png){width="72%" fig-align="center"}
:::
::::

![](/images/gr3.png){width="70%"}

**Graph (V,E):**

&nbsp;&nbsp; V: &emsp; \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

&nbsp;&nbsp; E: &emsp; \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

&nbsp;

**Complete Graph:**

[*A graph $G=(V,E)$ is* complete *iff $\forall u,v\in V,\;(u,v)\in E$.*]{style="color:#3c78d8; font-style:italic"}
:::

## Social Network {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="56%"}
![](/images/gr4.png){width="100%"}
:::
::: {.column width="44%"}
**Graph (V,E):**

&nbsp;&nbsp; V: &emsp; \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

&nbsp;&nbsp; E: &emsp; \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

&nbsp;

**Connected (sub)graph:** [*a (sub)graph $G=(V,E)$ is connected if there is a path from $u$ to $v$ $\forall u,v\in V$.*]{style="color:#3c78d8; font-style:italic; font-size:0.85em"}

**Connected Component:** [*a maximal connected subgraph.*]{style="color:#3c78d8; font-style:italic"}

**Spanning Tree:** [*connected, acyclic subgraph, containing all the vertices in $V$.*]{style="color:#3c78d8; font-style:italic"}
:::
::::

## Downtown Vancouver {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="58%"}
![](/images/downtownvan.png){width="100%"}
:::
::: {.column width="42%"}
**Graph (V,E):**

&nbsp;&nbsp; V: &emsp; \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

&nbsp;&nbsp; E: &emsp; \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

&nbsp;

**Directed Graph:** [*each edge $(u,v)$ is ordered — $(u,v) \neq (v,u)$. Streets like Howe (↓) and Seymour (↑) make this directed.*]{style="color:#3c78d8; font-style:italic; font-size:0.82em"}

**Weighted Graph:** [*each edge carries a weight $w(u,v)$ — here, travel time in minutes.*]{style="color:#3c78d8; font-style:italic; font-size:0.82em"}

**In/Out-degree(v):** [*\# edges directed into / out of $v$. A one-way intersection has in-degree $\neq$ out-degree.*]{style="color:#3c78d8; font-style:italic; font-size:0.82em"}

&nbsp;

*Fastest route: Seymour & Georgia → Burrard & Helmcken?*
:::

## Activity: Pencil Puzzles {.smaller}


::::: {.columns}
::: {.column}
You each have a graph. Do these three things:

1. Try to trace every edge exactly once without lifting your pencil. 

2. Come up with a rule that you can use to determine if a trace is possible.

3. Devise an algorithm that will find a trace if it exists.

:::
